According to a statement from Myanmar's Defense Ministry published in state media, the country announced on Sunday that it has taken legal action against dozens of people—including local officials—accused of extortion and illegal detention of men attempting to avoid compulsory military service. The ministry framed this as an effort to combat graft within the conscription process, representing what appears to be a rare official acknowledgement of corruption in Myanmar's draft system.

The statement emerges amid ongoing conflict: the military is engaged against pro-democracy rebels and ethnic minority factions in a civil war that began with the 2021 coup which removed Aung San Suu Kyi's democratically elected government. The text notes this acknowledgment as significant given the context of the nation being described as 'war-torn.'

The source material is limited to an official statement and does not provide specific details on the number or identities of those charged, nor independent verification of the claims.
items.title: Myanmar Reports Legal Action Against Officials Over Military Draft Corruption

items.summary: Ahmed al Ahmed, a fruit seller born in Syria who moved to Australia in 2006, recounted his experience tackling one of the gunmen during the mass shooting at a Jewish festival on Bondi Beach. The incident occurred when he was visiting the Sydney beach with his cousin and heard shots fired into a crowd as gunfire continued around him; al Ahmed rushed forward to tackle one gunman while others kept firing. Writing nearly a year after what is described as Australia's worst mass shooting in decades, he said his wounds still ache and issued a plea for unity.
items.title: Bondi shooting hero reflects on wounds and calls for unity nearly a year later

items.summary: Cricket Australia insists that its support for Pat Cummins to remain the Australian cricket captain is not an indication that it has chosen a side in the ongoing 'sandpaper' controversy. CA boss Todd Greenberg stated, "I am not putting someone's version of events over somebody else's," framing the backing as consistent with believing other players' accounts rather than dismissing them.
items.title: Cricket Australia says Cummins backing does not signal taking sides in sandpaper spat

items.summary: Australia's inaugural Recipe of the Year series concluded on its finale when Laura McLellan won the top prize for her Emerald Pie, a dish featuring green curry filling that references both her hometown in rural Queensland and its colour. The 36-year-old qualified nutritionist beat three home cook finalists—Jacqui Toumbas, Jimmy Stewart, and Ray Marouki—for the award after being judged by Country Women's Association judges Pia Miranda, Adam Liaw, and Ellice Schrader. McLellan grew up learning to cook from her mother, who immigrated with her father from Laos 40 years ago; she described winning as a surreal experience, noting she had not won an award since primary school. The three finalists praised the winner: Jimmy Stewart called McLellan's win deserved and likened the pie to humble pie on the outside with curry inside, Jacqui Toumbas described it as incredible and said many would recreate it at home, and Ray Marouki echoed that she had done an amazing job. The show was noted for its emphasis on accessible cooking using ingredients like frozen vegetables obtainable in regional areas, strong camaraderie among contestants, and the celebration of multiculturalism through diverse recipes.
items.title: Laura McLellan Wins ABC's Recipe of the Year with Emerald Pie

items.summary:
Toby Kiers, a biologist at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam and professor of Ecology and Evolution, became the youngest person to receive the 2026 Tyler Prize for Environmental Achievement. She was born in New York but raised in Connecticut before dropping out of college at 19; she later returned to study field biology after an internship that took her to a Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute station on an island in the Panama Canal, where she began studying mycorrhizal fungi—organisms associated with plant roots. Her research investigates how these brainless organisms make decisions and process information within underground networks.

Kiers reports that 90% of all plant species form connections with mycorrhizal fungi, and one study showed plants transfer roughly 13 billion tons of CO₂ annually to fungal networks—about one-third of fossil fuel emissions. She says the fungi use this carbon to build structures that hold soil together while supplying phosphorus and water to plants in deserts and arid zones.

She attributes much of the field's neglect to estimates that between two and three million fungal species exist on Earth with barely 1% identified, noting they are hard to see and short-lived. She describes threats including urban development, fungicides, agricultural intensification, and nitrogen from fertilizers in rainwater declining fungal diversity even in unmanaged forests.

In 2021 Kiers founded the Society for the Protection of Underground Networks (SPUN) to help secure international protections for underground fungi. SPUN created a subterranean atlas that identifies biodiversity hotspots using machine learning models fed by small grants awarded to scientists worldwide, and it maps uncertainty so predictions weaken with distance from actual samples. She reports 90% of hotspot locations fall outside currently protected areas—only about 10% have protection—and cites the Gobi Desert in Mongolia as an example of fungi surviving extreme conditions.

The article notes her team collaborates with AMOLF on imaging robots to track fungal development and decisions, and that one doctoral student studies whether flow patterns change over a day-night cycle. The text does not provide independent verification of Kiers's figures or the SPUN atlas statistics beyond what she states.
items.title: Toby Kiers Becomes Youngest Recipient of 2026 Tyler Prize for Research on Mycorrhizal Fungal Networks

items.summary: Netflix is streaming Gènesi, a six-episode Catalan-language series co-produced with 3Cat that chronicles Ferran Adrià's rise at El Bulli. The show premiered this fall; the chef describes it as potentially reaching a five-billion-person market while emphasizing its goal of relaunching what he calls the 'techno-emotional movement' in cooking, funded by the Generalitat to promote Catalonia and Spain. Adrià has accumulated 550 distinctions including three Michelin stars from 1997 until El Bulli closed in 2011, five-time best restaurant awards, six honorary doctorates (soon seven), a Chef of the Decade title, and recently the Gold Medal of Catalonia. The series dramatizes his career beginning when he joined as station chef in 1984 with no formal training, memorized El Practicón, then absorbed nouvelle cuisine from Jean-Paul Vinay's guidance on Bocuse and Guérard books; it also covers Joël Robuchon declaring Adrià the world's number one chef in 1996. Emotional arcs include Adrià's strained relationship with Santi Santamaría over molecular versus terroir cooking, his vow of silence during the 2008-2009 tabasco controversy involving then-prime minister José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero, and Juli Soler's Alzheimer's before dying in 2015. Adrià argues El Bulli drove much global innovation—claiming 'in twenty years we did 80% of the world's innovation!'—and that Spain communicates its cuisine poorly because it lacked a name for their approach while northern Europe developed New Nordic Cuisine; he sees hope in the government's International Plan for Spanish Gastronomy. The series is explicitly not critical reassessment, features actor Miquel Fernández as Adrià, and recreates dishes matching pages from Catálogo General de El Bulli.
items.title: Ferran Adrià's Netflix Series 'Gènesi' Premieres as He Reflects on El Bulli and Spain's Culinary Standing

items.summary: South Korean Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin resigned on Sunday over an AI-assisted cheating scandal that emerged days before the Suneung university entrance exam. The crisis began last Sunday when the top scorer in a national tax accountant exam admitted to using a miniature camera and smartphone to achieve a near-perfect score, just four days ahead of the nine-hour Suneung, which is widely regarded as a ticket to prestigious universities, well-paid jobs, and better marriage prospects. In response, officials rolled out preventive measures such as blocking public Wi-Fi in testing areas and placing stickers over clothing buttons; however, Choi struggled to reassure the public, particularly after remarks he made three days before the exam. Writing on X, Choi stated that although the Suneung concluded without major incidents, he failed to prepare adequately in advance and accepted full responsibility for his resignation, which President Lee Jae Myung had already accepted. During a parliamentary hearing on Monday, when asked whether authorities could catch would-be cheaters on exam day, the 72-year-old replied that due to his age he was not confident they could—a response that drew public backlash. Choi did not appear at press conferences in the days leading up to Thursday's exam, where a vice minister instead announced preventive measures. Officials reported that 111 cases of misconduct involving electronic devices were identified during the exam, with nearly half detected through three emergency alerts sent by the government to identify smartphones test takers had failed to hand over.
items.title: South Korea's Education Minister Resigns Over AI-Assisted Exam Cheating Scandal

items.summary: As Anthropic's internally named 'Project Lantern' IPO eclipsed SpaceX on Thursday, several people close to the process cited a litany of problems with the offering. These included a compressed timeline marred by last-minute changes, delays in sharing financial projections, rushed document approvals, and highly unusual restrictions on bankers amid concern about leaks—especially after Reuters reported details from a draft filing weeks before it was made public. Among these constraints, Anthropic instructed some of its 22 IPO underwriters to limit the number of bankers working on the deal to four senior staff members, likely out of fear that information would leak; one person said banks found ways to work around the restriction anyway. Underlying these complaints is a shifting power dynamic between technology companies and Wall Street: SpaceX, Anthropic—and potentially OpenAI—have come to wield enormous influence as AI demand drives frenzied interest in their shares, allowing them to dictate terms that upset some bankers while leaving those banks little choice but to comply. Both SpaceX and Anthropic debuted successfully with record amounts raised and oversubscribed order books; however, after an initial burst the two firms' trajectories diverged—SpaceX climbed to a post-listing peak of $201.80 on June 16 before retreating below its $135 IPO price in mid-July, while Anthropic's shares closed down 8.5% on Friday following a 17% first-day pop as the AI trade unraveled.
items.title: Anthropic's IPO Process Drawn Criticism for Unusual Restrictions and Delays

items.summary:
West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari said on Sunday that he would contact external affairs minister S Jaishankar after his office opened Monday to convey the state's concerns over escalating violence in neighbouring Bangladesh. He described the developments as 'extremely painful' and noted that around two crore people in West Bengal have relatives across the border, though he did not specify how the unrest had affected the state. Adhikari said he could write to the Centre seeking an extension of the December 31, 2024 cut-off date under which religious minorities from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan who entered India fleeing persecution are exempt from entry-document requirements; this exemption applies as amended in November 2026, with holders required to obtain a visa to remain. He cited protocol for not commenting directly on foreign affairs but said he would apprise Jaishankar of the public reaction if needed.

West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya separately urged people to set aside political differences and hold protests against the violence, arguing that Partition along religious lines contributed to the situation; he acknowledged the Centre would take appropriate decisions. The remarks follow escalating clashes between supporters of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) and the banned Awami League in several areas, prompting deployment of hundreds of additional paramilitary Border Guard Bangladesh personnel, alongside a 40-day nationwide protest launched Saturday by Jamaat-e-Islami, the main parliamentary opposition party, coinciding with planned return next month of deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina despite her death sentence.

The report reflects statements attributed to Adhikari and Bhattacharya rather than verified outcomes; it does not establish how effectively any extension request would be received or whether protests would materialise.
items.title: West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari to Contact Jaishankar Over Bangladesh Violence and Possible Extension of Minority Entry Cut-off

items.summary: Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav, who led India's delegation at the UN climate conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkiye, stated that the absence of a cover decision from the meeting does not pause India's domestic climate action. He emphasized that the country continues to deliver on its commitments and remains committed to consensus-based multilateralism as it moves toward COP32, scheduled for Ethiopia in 2027. As supporting evidence of ongoing progress, Yadav cited India's expanding renewable energy capacity, noting solar power installations have exceeded 170 GW. The report is attributed to Vishwa Mohan, Senior Editor at The Times of India, who covers environment and climate policy issues.
items.title: India's Environment Minister Says Missing COP31 Cover Decision Won't Halt Climate Progress

items.summary: A New York Times report published on Saturday alleges that China's Ministry of State Security (MSS) has made acquiring advanced semiconductor chips a priority, running an effort for at least two years to overcome Western export restrictions. The MSS established a working group under its chief Chen Yixin to lead the campaign, which reportedly includes helping Chinese companies acquire and smuggle advanced chips into the country, collecting intelligence on the global chip industry and its supply chains, and gathering data on the semiconductor sector. According to officials cited by the report from Asia, the US, and Europe, this effort is part of a broader push led by President Xi Jinping toward technological self-reliance, coordinated at the party level by the Central Science and Technology Commission—established in 2023 and headed by Politburo Standing Committee member Ding Xuexiang. Chen Yixin became China's state security minister in late 2022 and has repeatedly framed opposition to Western technology restrictions as a core responsibility of his agency, calling for intensified efforts against technological blockades in April. The report coincides with US scrutiny of Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, whom American officials allege worked with the MSS to spy on Jensen Huang, Nvidia's co-founder; earlier NYT reporting from November 20 detailed indirect links between companies tied to Huang's family and state-owned defence contractors supplying the People's Liberation Army (PLA). That investigation cited a confidential analysis by Strider Technologies alongside corporate filings, finding roughly USD 3.6 billion in Chinese government funding flowed through companies associated with Huang's family or business associates—funding technology projects including data centres that received Nvidia chips—but did not establish whether the military actually used computing power from those facilities. Alice Huang operated Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data centre company under US Justice Department investigation for suspected illegal advanced-chip shipments to China; her sister Huang Yu and investor Kang Wei held stakes in companies such as Shanghai's Century Litong (founded 2023 by Century Longteng) and Jiangsu Lettall Electronic. The report notes the Trump administration announced a rule requiring overseas data centres to obtain government licences before supplying significant computing power to companies headquartered in countries including China, Russia, and Iran, with restrictions set to take effect about 90 days after announcement.
items.title: NYT Report: China's Ministry of State Security Ran Multi-Year Campaign to Acquire Advanced Chips and Gather Semiconductor Intelligence

items.summary: A Delta outage involving the automated system used to calculate aircraft weight and balance triggered delays across multiple U.S. airports just days before Thanksgiving, one of the busiest travel periods in the United States. The FAA initially issued a ground stop for Delta flights heading to Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport on Sunday morning; it was later downgraded to a ground delay that allowed departures but required longer waits and was expected to remain in effect until at least 1 p.m. ET, with flights to Atlanta facing an average delay of nearly an hour according to Atlanta News First. Delta attributed the disruption to its automation system failure, which handles weight-and-balance calculations essential before takeoff; because the system malfunctioned, employees used manual procedures and workarounds to prepare aircraft for departure while coordinating with air traffic control to protect gates and tarmac areas from congestion at the Atlanta hub. The outage extended beyond Atlanta, affecting flights at Newark Liberty International Airport, LaGuardia Airport, Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, Washington Dulles International Airport, Boston Logan International Airport, Baltimore/Washington International Airport, Miami International Airport, Minneapolis–Saint Paul International Airport, and Nashville International Airport. According to Patch, 1,010 Delta flights—about 30% of the airline's scheduled flights—were delayed as of 11:30 a.m. ET on Sunday, November 22, with Atlanta recording more delays than any other airport. The disruption added pressure during an already busy holiday period; Hartsfield-Jackson officials expect more than 4 million passengers through December 1, up about 5% from the previous year.
items.title: Delta automation failure delayed more than 1,000 US flights ahead of Thanksgiving

items.summary:
Railway cleaning staff aboard the New Delhi–Varanasi Vande Bharat Express (train 22416) discovered an unattended black bag during routine maintenance at the train's yard after it reached its destination on Friday, prompting a return of belongings to their owner. Attendant Anoop Kumar and cleaner Karan Singh spotted the bag in Coach E1 near seat number 35 once the train arrived at Varanasi Junction; passenger Lim Weng Shang had accidentally left one bag behind after alighting there with his guide.

The contents, verified by Railway Protection Force (RPF) Sub-Inspector Charan Singh and deputy station superintendent Vakil Singh in the presence of station director Arpit Gupta on Saturday, totaled ₹2.11 lakh in Indian currency plus foreign cash: $1,000, 1,22,000 Sri Lankan rupees, and 66 Singapore dollars.

Shang returned to Cantt railway station with his guide after realizing the loss; officials verified his identity before handing over all belongings intact. Shang praised Indian Railways for its honesty and prompt response. The report is attributed to TOI, while a Livemint News Desk boilerplate about coverage areas appears at the end of the source.
items.title: Vande Bharat staff found and returned a tourist's bag containing ₹2.11 lakh and foreign currency

items.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) announced on November 22, 2026 that it has granted sanctions to launch prosecution under the FSS Act against five companies for violations tied to non-compliant regulatory samples. In Bisleri International's case, a sample was found unsafe due to exceeding prescribed bromate limits and also tested positive for polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) after referral to the Referral Food Lab. Vasant Masala Pvt Ltd faced sanctions because its chilli powder sample was declared unsafe even by the Referral Lab; Tit-Bit Foods' pre-packaged turmeric and chilli powders were found unsafe due to pesticide residues above permissible limits; and Mimansa Industries Pvt Ltd's walnut kernels sample was also deemed unsafe. FSSAI stated that prosecution sanctions had been granted against all five companies, though no specific details on penalties or timelines for the proceedings are provided.
items.title: FSSAI Sanctions Prosecution Against Five Companies Over Unsafe Food Samples

items.summary:
As winter approaches year-end, several Indian railway operators are promoting scenic Vande Bharat routes for holiday travel. The article presents five specific routes with schedules, fares, and landscape highlights as reported by Livemint—News Desk.

The Delhi–Katra route connects New Delhi to the gateway of the Vaishno Devi shrine; train 22439 departs at 6 am and arrives at 2 pm (return train 22440 leaves Katra at 3 pm, arriving in New Delhi at 11 pm), with chair car fares from ₹1,630 and executive chair car at ₹3,015. The Bengaluru–Goa route runs as train 26655 leaving Yesvantpur Junction at 7:35 am and reaching Madgaon at 8:55 pm after halting at 12 stations; per a report by The Hindu, AC Chair Car fares are approximately ₹1,369 and Executive Chair Car ₹2,795, inclusive of base price, reservation/superfast charges, and 5% GST. The Delhi–Dehradun route covers 302 km in about 4 hours 45 minutes on all days except Wednesdays (train 22457 departs Anand Vihar at 17:50), with AC Chair Car fares of ₹1,065 and executive chair car ₹1,890. The Katra–Srinagar route was introduced in 2026 as part of expanded Kashmir railway network; trains 26401/26402 (Katra to Srinagar via Banihal) run except Tuesdays while 26403/26404 operate except Wednesdays, highlighting the Chenab Rail Bridge at 359 metres above the riverbed. The Howrah–Puri route offers AC Chair Car fares of ₹1,430 (including ₹328 catering) and executive chair car ₹2,615 (₹389 catering), while train 22895 charges ₹1,265 (₹162 catering) and ₹2,420 (₹195 catering); food is optional with a 'No Food Option' that omits the catering charge.

The article's figures are presented as reported schedules and fares without independent verification. Several details carry uncertainty: the Delhi–Katra fare appears to be for New Delhi to Katra, while the Bengaluru–Goa schedule lists Yesvantpur Junction (Bengaluru) rather than a literal Bengaluru station; the Katra–Srinagar route is described as introduced in 2026, which may reflect future or planned service. The piece also includes an unrelated boilerplate description of Livemint—News Desk's coverage areas and staff.
items.title: Scenic Vande Bharat Routes to Explore This Winter: Delhi–Vaishno Devi, Bengaluru–Goa and Others

items.summary: Dr. Louis Bherer, a professor at Université de Montréal and director of the EPIC Centre at Montreal Heart Institute, argues that lifestyle habits—not just molecular cures—could substantially reduce dementia risk, potentially preventing nearly half (45%) of cases through 14 identified modifiable risk factors. This prevention factor has been neglected by public health authorities despite billions being spent on Alzheimer's research.
items.title: Healthy Lifestyle Habits Could Prevent Up to 45% of Dementia Cases

items.summary: A car carrying 10 people crashed into a neem tree near Kothurpatty four-road junction in Tiruchirappalli district on Sunday evening around 4 pm, killing eight and leaving two seriously injured. The occupants were returning to Thirukattupalli in Thanjavur district after attending an ear-piercing ceremony at Erumapatti in Namakkal district. Five people died at the scene while three others later succumbed to their injuries at Musiri Government Hospital; police identified all eight deceased and named the two injured, Ramalingam and Ramar, who remain hospitalized.
items.title: Car Crash Kills 8 in Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu

items.summary: Following reports that two individuals developed kidney disease after using skin-lightening creams, Kerala Health Minister K Muraleedharan ordered a statewide inspection of unapproved cosmetics and protein powders. The claims came from 17-year-old girl Saleem Kodathoor (a singer), who reported suffering membranous nephropathy about 10 years ago, and another individual whose doctors said her body contained high mercury levels after using a cream with dangerous quantities of the chemical. In response, Muraleedharan directed the State Drugs Controller to inspect all districts, targeting face sheets, skin-lightening products, tone-improving creams, pills, ointments, salves, and other cosmetics marketed through false advertisements promising muscle strength or physical enhancement. The order also calls for scrutiny of online sales and distribution networks, permanent cancellation of licences for establishments selling illegal products, criminal proceedings against responsible parties, monitoring of social media vloggers who promote such items, and legal action against paid promoters. Muraleedharan stated that unapproved beauty and health products are being imported into Kerala from Pakistan and the Mangaluru-Kasaragod region, with some lacking basic manufacturer details; he warned doctors had cautioned that fake or unsafe products could harm the kidneys, liver, nervous system, and cause skin cancer. The minister advised consumers to use such products only under authorised medical guidance and to verify product approvals rather than being swayed by advertisements promising quick results.
items.title: Kerala Orders Statewide Crackdown on Unapproved Cosmetics and Protein Powders After Kidney Disease Claims

items.summary: According to a report published by the Daily Mail, based on claims from royal journalist Tom Sykes in his forthcoming book 'The Dukes: Edward VIII, Andrew, and Harry — the Men Who Undermined the Modern Monarchy,' Prince William is reportedly planning significant changes to the British monarchy that could result in Prince Harry, Meghan Markle, and their two children losing their royal titles upon William's accession. Sykes quotes a source close to the Prince of Wales stating that future royals would receive titles such as HRH and prince or princess only if they performed public duties including official tours, diplomatic work, and government engagements; those who did not undertake such roles would instead become private citizens free to pursue independent careers without royal accommodation or special privileges. The source reportedly added that working royals would additionally receive an allowance or salary. Under this proposed framework, William's younger children—Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis—would be permitted to choose between becoming working royals or pursuing independent careers, while his eldest son, Prince George, as heir apparent, would retain a predetermined role. These reported plans align with statements made by William during an interview on Apple TV+'s 'The Reluctant Traveler,' in which he described change as being on his agenda and expressed willingness to modernize the institution while preserving relevant traditions. The report references Harry and Meghan's 2020 departure from royal duties and relocation to California, following their estrangement from William and other family members. Representatives for Harry and Meghan were unavailable for comment, while a spokesperson for William and Kate Middleton declined to address claims made in books or publications as policy. Kensington Palace has not officially confirmed the reported proposal.
items.title: Prince William reportedly plans to strip Prince Harry and Meghan of royal titles

items.summary: Following a threat email received on November 21, Hyderabad police stepped up security across the city on Sunday while dismissing the message as likely work of a mischief-monger. On Saturday, an alert issued by the joint commissioner (special branch) to all police stations stated that the department had received an email titled 'Lashkar-e-Taiba,' in which the sender threatened a 26/11-style terror attack on Hyderabad to avenge the killing of terrorist Lateef Bhat in Kulgam, Jammu and Kashmir. The email named Hotel Tourist Plaza in Kachiguda and Kachiguda railway station as targets for bomb blasts intended to kill hundreds in retaliation for the Indian Army's operation against Bhat and his associates. Police sources said the email, purportedly sent by LeT, put the force on alert with all police stations instructed to increase vigilance; the named sites plus several other crowded places were searched but no explosives were found. In a Sunday statement, Hyderabad police reported that anti-sabotage checks had been conducted at suspected locations and visible policing intensified for public safety, while cybercrime police investigated to trace the sender. The department appealed to citizens not to believe or spread rumors and asked them to dial 112 if they spotted suspicious persons or unattended objects.
items.title: Hyderabad steps up security after threat email linked to Lateef Bhat killing

items.summary:
The BJP accused the Tamil Nadu government of an "anti-Hindu and anti-Sanatan Dharma" mindset after the state's Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department commissioner filed a review petition in the Supreme Court. The review was sought following the court's Friday order permitting the one-time lighting of the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp on November 24 at Deepathoon, a stone pillar atop Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai.

BJP spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi characterized the government's move as an attempt to avoid implementing the Supreme Court judgment, describing it as reflecting both "anti-constitutional" and religiously hostile intentions. BJP Rajya Sabha MP Ravi Shankar Prasad echoed these charges, alleging that the action demonstrates the Congress and its allies' "hatred against Hindu Dharma," while demanding immediate implementation of the court's ruling.

The Tamil Nadu government operates under a TVK-led coalition in which the Congress is an alliance partner. The article notes a related development regarding medical, food safety, and crowd control measures announced for the Tiruvannamalai Karthigai Deepam event.
items.title: BJP Accuses Tamil Nadu Government of 'Anti-Hindu' Mindset Over Supreme Court Review Plea on Karthigai Deepam

items.summary:
Within six months of assuming power, factional tensions within Congress's Kerala unit escalated to the national level when a group of leaders—including Lok Sabha MP Rajmohan Unnithan—met AICC president Mallikarjun Kharge in Delhi. The complainants belong to the 'A' group, previously led by AK Antony and later Oommen Chandy (who died in July 2023), which had weakened before reportedly resurfacing under current leadership.

The leaders relayed grievances about lack of coordination between party and government, delayed appointment of a full-time state unit president, insufficient consultation on board and corporation appointments, and exclusion from internal forums on policy issues. They noted that most senior KPCC members hold cabinet positions while Sunny Joseph simultaneously serves as Power Minister, leaving no dedicated organizational oversight.

The meeting followed similar complaints from UDF convenor Adoor Prakash about absent coalition meetings; the AICC had not formally acted on his submission. KPCC president Sunny Joseph stated he would meet AICC leadership later that month and emphasized major issues should be discussed internally before government announcements, while Unnithan highlighted the absence of an internal grievance mechanism.

Conversely, health minister K Muraleedharan—perceived as close to Chief Minister VD Satheesan—defended the administration's record, arguing positive achievements are being underreported amid factional disputes and that government operations remain systematic. The report is based on statements from anonymous sources and party figures; no formal AICC action has been taken on any of the grievances raised.
items.title: Congress Factional Rift Deepens in Kerala as Dissenting Leaders Air Grievances with National President Kharge

items.summary: This text is a personal tribute by Sreekala Sivasankaran, who shared approximately 25 years of friendship with the late playwright and theatre personality Omcherry NN Pillai. The author recounts that Pillai was born in Vaikom, Kerala, in 1924 into a humble Nair family; he nearly lost his place at school due to unpaid fees but continued after securing a scholarship whose results arrived before the teacher intervened by paying on time—an episode Pillai later described as serendipitous boons. He pursued diverse studies including Vedanta philosophy, Arabic and Islamic studies, law, mass communication at University College in Kerala, advanced degrees at the University of Pennsylvania and New Mexico State University, and a faculty position at the Indian Institute of Mass Communication in Delhi. His career included founding the Delhi Experimental Theatre in 1963 as a platform for socially relevant drama; authoring nine plays and more than 80 one-act plays; receiving the Kerala Sahitya Akademi Award for lifetime work in 2010, the Kerala Prabha Award from the state government in 2022, and the Sahitya Akademi Award in 2020 for his memoir Aakasmikam. The author notes that Pillai designed the Congress's Garibi Hatao campaign artwork with Makhan Dasgupta during the 1970s while teaching at IIMC; this information remained a public secret until recently revealed through the memoir, which he wrote without taking remuneration because of his government service. The tribute highlights Pralayam as Pillai's most enduring creation: first written as a poem, then an English TV play, and developed into a full-length Malayalam play in 1970; it won the Kerala Sahitya Akademi Award in 1972 and was staged at Bharat Rang Mahotsav events including one in January 2006. The author acted as Miss Mary—a character interpreted by poet Satchidanandan as Christ—in a recreation directed by Samkutty Pattomkary, with Delhi actor Anilkumar and Sajitha Madathil playing Noah figures; former President KR Narayanan attended an early performance under Janasanskriti at the National School of Drama. The author frames Pillai's message about nuclear threats, war, human greed, and media manipulation as perpetually relevant amid ongoing conflicts such as Ukraine and Gaza. Because he transcended political factions—described by friends as belonging only to theatre, arts, literature, Malayalam, and universal humanism—the family was affectionately called Delhi's 'Malayali Bagh.' The tribute offers no biographical dates of death or formal limitations beyond the author's personal perspective.
items.title: Remembering Playwright Omcherry NN Pillai: A Humanist Legacy in Delhi's Cultural Life

items.summary: An awareness rally was held on Sunday in Hanamkonda, Warangal, to promote natural deliveries and reduce unnecessary Caesarean sections. Around 700 nursing students participated in the event, which was jointly organised by the Society of Midwives, India (SOMI) and a government nursing college. District collector Chahat Bajpai and police commissioner Swetha flagged off the rally, after which participants walked from the KMC Arch to the Government Maternity Hospital while raising slogans and displaying placards about natural childbirth, safe motherhood, and midwifery services. Speakers emphasised providing pregnant women with proper medical advice during pregnancy and strengthening midwifery services, arguing that such awareness could build confidence among expectant mothers and their families in natural childbirth. Students distributed pamphlets explaining the benefits of natural deliveries, pregnancy precautions, and safe motherhood, and the programme concluded with participants taking a pledge to promote natural childbirth, provide compassionate midwifery care, and ensure safe motherhood for all. The text reports only on this single event; it does not present delivery statistics or evidence that unnecessary Caesarean sections are actually occurring at measurable rates.
items.title: Awareness Rally Promotes Natural Deliveries in Hanamkonda

items.summary: During his November 20-22 visit to New Delhi for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Civilisational Dialogue Forum, Pakistan's Climate Change Minister Musadik Masood Malik reported that he had not been invited for bilateral talks with Indian officials. Speaking in Delhi on November 22, Malik stated that any discussion of contentious issues would require a formal invitation and an established mechanism, noting that "without a mechanism" such discussions cannot occur. His visit was described as strictly multilateral; while he held bilateral meetings with Tajikistan and Iran representatives, no engagement took place with Indian counterparts. Malik indicated willingness to discuss specific topics if India initiated dialogue, including the Indus Waters Treaty, which he said had not been formally invited for discussion at that time. On terrorism, he argued discussions should be evidence-based rather than provocation-driven, claiming Pakistan had repeatedly offered bilateral or multilateral platforms for such talks. Separately, while Indian authorities approved Malik's request to visit security-cleared sites including the Taj Mahal in Agra and Humayun's Tomb in Delhi, his request to visit the Hazrat Nizamuddin Dargah was denied on security grounds according to India's Ministry of External Affairs.
items.title: Pakistan Climate Minister Says He Was Not Invited for Bilateral Talks With India

items.summary: United Nations climate negotiations held at COP31 in Antalya, Turkiye, failed on Sunday to produce an overarching agreement after several countries and the 27-nation European Union rejected a final proposal that made no explicit mention of fossil fuels. The talks ran nearly 48 hours overtime before collapsing without a main 'cover decision,' though negotiators noted progress had been made on smaller issues during the two-week session. Any pact at these negotiations requires near-unanimous consensus, and while Russia and Saudi Arabia pushed to keep fossil fuels out of the document, a larger number of nations accepted the deal—often reluctantly—prioritizing reaching some form of consensus over content they found insufficient. EU Climate Minister Darragh O'Brien condemned the outcome as 'unconscionable,' arguing it was unacceptable for a climate act to omit any reference to fossil fuels, which he identified as the chief cause of global warming. The impasse reflects a broader pattern: UN climate outcomes generally avoided explicitly naming fossil fuels during most of the first 25 years of negotiations until three years ago, when an agreement in the United Arab Emirates called for 'transitioning away from fossil fuels.' Since that Dubai deal, no explicit mention has appeared; the Turkish-Australian leadership proposal recalled it but did not satisfy many nations and environmental groups. The article notes that despite the failure on the cover decision, discussions continued afterward.
items.title: UN Climate Talks in Antalya Fail to Reach Fossil Fuel Agreement

items.summary: In an ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 match on Sunday, India A captain Tilak Varma reached a fighting fifty off 95 deliveries with three boundaries against Pakistan A in a high-pressure chase of 314 runs. His knock came at a critical juncture when India A had slipped to 177/6 after 34.5 overs; the team's batting lineup otherwise struggled, as Abhishek Sharma had earlier provided an explosive start with 70 off 42 balls while others failed to build partnerships. With wickets falling at regular intervals and India A needing 137 runs from 91 deliveries remaining, Varma's presence was described as crucial for holding the innings together. At the time of reporting, Shahbaz Ahmed batted alongside him on 24 off 25 balls, with both players tasked with keeping India's hopes alive in the contest.
items.title: Tilak Varma Scores Fighting Fifty to Anchor India A Chase Against Pakistan A

items.summary: Oscar-winning composer AR Rahman revealed at a press conference during the International Film Festival of India on Sunday (November 22) that he spent nearly three years composing music for Nitesh Tiwari's two-part adaptation of Ramayana. During this period, he turned down approximately 10 to 12 film projects, including work with several prominent filmmakers, in order to remain focused on the project. Rahman composed alongside German composer Hans Zimmer and stated that some tracks underwent more than a dozen versions before finalization; specifically, 'Ravana Tandav' reportedly went through 12-13 iterations until the team settled on a version everyone liked. He expressed pride in his commitment while explaining that he only accepts projects he genuinely loves because they nourish his artistic sense and energize his team. Rahman also discussed balancing traditional Indian sounds with modern global influences, describing himself as multicultural and noting that combining these styles can be confusing but enjoyable to explore.
items.title: AR Rahman Dedicates Three Years to Ramayana Music, Turns Down 10-12 Films

items.summary: Delhi Traffic Police issued traffic advisories for Monday in connection with two events marking the Prakash Gurpurab of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji: a VIP movement at Rajghat (Mahatma Gandhi's memorial) and a Nagar Kirtan procession organized by the Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee. The police stated that restrictions would be enforced near Rajghat from 10 am to 11 am, contingent on VIP movement and traffic conditions, with diversions potentially imposed at ITO Chowk, Delhi Gate, Guru Nanak Chowk, Shantivan Chowk, Rajghat DTC Depot, and IP Flyover. Special arrangements were also announced for north Delhi from 3 pm onward, affecting BSZ Marg between ITO Chowk and Delhi Gate, the Ring Road between Shantivan Chowk and IP Flyover, Asaf Ali Road between Delhi Gate and Netaji Subhash Marg, Nishad Raj Marg from Shantivan Chowk, and Ranjit Singh Flyover from Guru Nanak Chowk. The Nagar Kirtan procession was scheduled to run from Gurudwara Sis Ganj Sahib in Chandni Chowk to Gurudwara Nanak Piao Sahib on GT Karnal Road, passing through a listed set of central Delhi locations including Fatehpuri, Khari Baoli, Naya Bazar Chowk, Peeli Kothi Road, Pul Mithai, Zorawar Singh Marg, Barf Khana Chowk, and Roshanara Road. The police noted that curbs along the procession route would depend on its movement, with impacts potentially extending to additional stretches such as Town Hall, Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Marg, Qutub Road Chowk, Pul Dufferin, Rani Jhansi Flyover, Sabzi Mandi, and Roop Nagar. The police urged commuters to plan journeys in advance, allow extra travel time, and avoid affected routes during the advisory periods.
items.title: Delhi Traffic Police Issue Advisories for Guru Nanak Jayanti VIP Movement and Nagar Kirtan on Monday

items.summary:
At a media briefing in Delhi during his visit for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) dialogue, Pakistan Minister Musadik Masood Malik declined to address questions on terrorism and the Indus Waters Treaty, stating he had not been invited by India for any bilateral talks. He said that without a formal mechanism or an explicit invitation from India, there is no basis for discussing bilateral issues, adding: "When you invite me for a discussion on those specific issues, I shall be there." Malik emphasized his visit was focused solely on the multilateral SCO meeting and not on bilateral engagement with India.

On terrorism, he said the matter could be addressed through evidence-based dialogue via bilateral or multilateral platforms, noting that both countries have suffered losses. He stated Pakistan has repeatedly offered to present its evidence in various forums, saying: "You bring your evidence, and we will bring ours." Regarding the Indus Waters Treaty, Malik repeated his position that he would discuss it only if India extended an invitation.

The report presents these statements as reported by the Pakistani minister; no independent verification of whether India issued any such invitations is provided in the text.
items.title: Pakistan minister declines bilateral questions, citing lack of Indian invitation
